seed_ledger.name: Waha to Mexico (Wahalajara System Expansion)
seed_ledger.reason: Expansion is two compressor units in Chihuahua and Aguascalientes, Mexico, about 1.3 to 2 Bcf/d. Esentia lists data centers only as a Mexican demand sector. No new US pipe and no US data center tie. Sources checked: trade press (Pipeline and Gas Journal, Inspenet) showed the Mexican compression scope; a Waha/Trans-Pecos search showed no US expansion tied to it. EIA row, FERC, Railroad Commission not re-searched beyond earlier pass. Searches run: 2.

evidence.note: Phase II compression at San Juan and Aguascalientes, Mexico; data centers named as sector

seed_ledger.name: Bulldog Power Plant (gas supply)
seed_ledger.reason: NOT_FOUND on gas supply. New finding: the plant is the colocated power for Nightpeak Energy's Old Ocean Data Center near Sweeny (two 310 MW data centers plus two 310 MW turbine plants, 158 acres, energize 2027, Bulldog turbine in development since 2023); Brazoria County denied tax abatements in March 2026. Data center tie is now sourced, but no source names the gas supplier, a lateral or length. NGPL and Old Ocean Pipeline run within 2 km, so a tap is likely but unsourced. Sources checked: Bisnow showed project scope; The Facts article (Mar 2026) confirmed Bulldog as developer; data center tracker lists 620 MW; TCEQ and trade press searches showed no supply deal. Searches run: 6.

evidence.note: Nightpeak Old Ocean Data Center with colocated Bulldog Power turbines at Sweeny

seed_ledger.name: Data City Energy Center (gas supply)
seed_ledger.reason: NOT_FOUND on gas supply. Data City is a planned 5 GW campus near Laredo, first phase 300 MW, off-grid, starting on on-site gas turbines later moving to hydrogen from neighboring Hydrogen City. Data center tie is real but no pipeline, supplier or tap is named; nearest GGIT route is Tejas 6 km away. Sources checked: DCD and Bisnow described the power plan; Webb County well records and plant searches showed nothing relevant. Searches run: 3.

evidence.note: Data City 5 GW campus near Laredo, gas turbines first

seed_ledger.name: NextEra Comstock power station (gas supply)
seed_ledger.reason: No dedicated gas lateral found for the NextEra and Comstock plant near Bethel in Anderson County. A Comstock press release from March 2026 says the gas comes from the Western Haynesville, nearly 1 billion cubic feet a day by 2031, and points to transmission infrastructure at Bethel. A KLTV report on the April 2026 county commissioners meeting says there are no current data center plans and only a possible future tie. NextEra's April 2026 materials call the load a potential large industrial customer. A Standard and Poor's interview from September 2026 puts the plant next to the Trinity Gas Storage hub, but that page could not be read, so only its search summary was seen. No pipeline name, length or filing was found. The EIA pipeline projects table has no entry for Anderson County. A search of federal prior notice filings found nothing for the county. Searches run: 11. Sources checked: Comstock press release, KLTV, Data Center Dynamics on the NextEra federal approval, Natural Gas Intelligence, Utility Dive, Oil and Gas Journal on the Comstock midstream deal, Standard and Poor's summary, the EIA table, a FERC filing search, and a Railroad Commission search, which showed no T-4 or tap filing.

evidence.note: source cited in the seed agent's reason

seed_ledger.name: Socorro power station (gas supply)
seed_ledger.reason: ONSITE_NO_PIPE: Atlas Energy Solutions signed a five-year power agreement for a 120 MW private plant at Socorro, Texas, reportedly for the Wiwynn factories. It is off-grid and run on gas engines. The GOGPT notes cite a TCEQ review calling it behind-the-meter. No source says where the gas comes from, and no new pipe was found. Wiwynn makes data center equipment, so the data center tie is also weak. The El Paso Meta lateral (P8316) is a different site. Searches run: 8. Checked: Atlas 8-K of March 2026 (power agreement, energization first half of 2027, no gas supply stated); El Paso Times and Reuters syndication on Wiwynn (120 MW off-grid plant replacing 13 portable generators, no gas source); Aterio listing (gas reciprocating engines, early 2027); TCEQ public notices and permit search (nothing found); EIA, FERC, Railroad Commission and county records (nothing found).

evidence.note: Atlas 8-K, five-year power purchase agreement, energization first half of 2027, no gas supply named
